summary: Dashboard tile refresh stalls when query cache lock persists, causing delayed trace links and alert delivery
description: Issue summary: Several customers reported dashboard tiles in the Console stalling on refresh for up to 30+ seconds. Stalled tiles show a spinning loader; clicking through trace links either returns 404 or times out until the tile finally completes. Impact: Multiple enterprise customers (Streamline AI + 2 others) reported missing alerts or delayed alert delivery tied to dashboard rule evaluation. Environment: prod, us-east, Console version 3.14.2, query-cache-service v1.7.2. Expected behavior: Dashboard tiles should refresh within configured panel timeout (default 3s) and trace links should remain stable. Actual behavior: Tile hangs until a cache lock TTL expires (~25-35s); during that time associated alert evaluations are queued and can miss the evaluation window, causing delayed or dropped alerts.
steps_to_reproduce: Open Console -> Dashboards -> Organization X -> Panel 'Request Latency (p95)'
Trigger a high-cardinality ad-hoc query (example filter: route:*/batch, user_agent:mobile*)
Initiate a refresh (manual or automatic) while a background compaction job is running on the query-cache node
Observe tile spinner remains for 20-40 seconds; clicking trace link either times out or returns 404 until tile completes
logs:
Selected logs from query-cache (us-east-1) around 2026-03-10T14:02:34Z: 
[query-cache] WARN lock_acquire: key=panel:orgX:queryHash: ttl_override=30000ms owner=compactor-3
[dashboard-renderer] ERROR tile_render_timeout: panel_id=428 path=/dashboards/panel/428 waiting_for=cache_lock
[alert-eval] WARN evaluation_delayed: rule_id=547 queued_for=28000ms
Tracebacks: dashboard-renderer timed out waiting on cache lock; subsequent re-eval succeeded at 2026-03-10T14:03:06Z
investigation_notes: Hypotheses: (1) Cache compaction/rehash job temporarily extends lock TTL beyond expected values, (2) Lock cleanup job not running due to recent deployment, (3) Dashboard renderer mishandles lock wait backoff. Findings: Replayed compaction schedule correlated with spike in long-held locks on query-cache nodes. Lock TTLs increased to 30s due to regression in compaction job (PR linked). Dashboard renderer waits for lock without exponential backoff and does not surface immediate fallback causing spinner and delayed trace link resolution. Metrics: lock_hold_time 95th percentile jumped from 120ms -> 28s during compaction window. No signs of database contention. Affected customers all in us-east region using org-scoped high-cardinality queries.
comments: Support (2026-03-10) - Aisha Patel: Customer reports multiple dashboard tiles stalling and missing alerts. Reproduced in prod/us-east. Escalating to SRE and Console owners.

SRE (2026-03-10) - Priya Nair: Observed lock_hold_time spike on query-cache; pointed to compaction PR (https://github.com/redwood-inference/cache/pull/402). Temporarily disabled compaction on us-east to mitigate.
Console Eng (2026-03-11) - Marco Velez: Identified renderer wait loop that blocks for full TTL without fallback. Preparing patch to add fast-fail and fall back to best-effort execution path.
Customer (2026-03-11) - Streamline AI (Ben Carter): Confirmed tiles returned to normal after compaction disabled; reported one missed alert. Requesting postmortem and assurance this won't recur.
Support (2026-03-12) - Aisha Patel: Deployed hotfix to reduce compaction lock TTL and added renderer fallback. Added alerting rule for lock_hold_time > 5s. Marking resolved pending postmortem.
SRE (2026-03-12) - Priya Nair: Follow-up: Re-enabled compaction with adjusted settings; monitoring shows no recurrence in 24h window.
resolution: Mitigation: Disabled compaction on affected query-cache cluster and cleared stale locks. Deployed hotfixs: (1) query-cache compaction PR rolled back and TTL reduced, (2) console renderer updated to fast-fail after 2s and render partial results with informative tooltip, (3) alerting rule added for lock_hold_time > 5s and an incident dashboard for cache metrics. Follow-up: Postmortem page created, and a small migration scheduled to add lock ownership metadata to improve cleanup. Customer notified and credited for partial SLA impact.
